skill.name: threejs-materials
skill.description: Choosing and configuring three.js materials - unlit, diffuse, specular, PBR, toon, point and line materials - shared properties like blending and stencil, environment response, and the WebGPU node-material and TSL equivalents. Use when styling meshes or tuning material behavior.
skill.summary: Choose and tune three.js materials, texture channels, environment lighting, and WebGPU node materials with examples targeting r186.
skill.author: cloudai-x

content.value_statement: Incorrect material settings can cause dark surfaces, washed-out textures, and transparency artifacts. This skill provides material selection guidance and examples for three.js r186.
actual_capabilities: Compare unlit, diffuse, specular, PBR, toon, point, line, and custom shader materials.
Configure roughness, metalness, transmission, clearcoat, sheen, and other physical surface properties.
Explain texture color spaces, packed ORM channels, and UV channel selection.
Show blending, stencil masking, depth settings, and geometry groups for multiple materials.
Guide environment lighting, runtime material changes, cloning, disposal, and rendering performance.
Provide WebGPU setup, TSL node-material examples, and renderer compatibility guidance.
limitations: The skill is a Markdown reference, not an executable renderer or automated visual testing tool.
Examples target three.js r186; other releases can require API changes.
Referenced textures and HDR environment files are not included.
GLSL ShaderMaterial examples target WebGLRenderer; WebGPU custom shading requires node materials and TSL.

use_cases.title: Configure Product Surfaces
use_cases.description: Choose PBR materials for metal, lacquer, fabric, and glass in an interactive product viewer.

use_cases.title: Debug Material Appearance
use_cases.description: Review lighting, texture color spaces, UV channels, and transparency settings when a scene renders incorrectly.

use_cases.title: Plan WebGPU Material Migration
use_cases.description: Identify renderer compatibility limits and translate custom shading concepts into TSL node materials.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Basic Material
prompt_templates.prompt: I am using three.js r186. Recommend a material for [surface] with [lighting conditions]. Explain the choice and show a minimal example.

prompt_templates.title: Configure PBR Textures
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure MeshStandardMaterial for [model] using [available textures]. Explain color spaces, packed ORM channels, and UV selection. Assume three.js r186.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Rendering Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [material and renderer setup] for [visible artifact]. Check transparency, depth writing, blending, lighting, and recompilation requirements. Propose focused fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Custom Shading
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt [WebGL ShaderMaterial effect] to three.js r186 WebGPURenderer using TSL. Identify node slots, imports, initialization requirements, and renderer limitations.

output_examples.input: My textured PBR model looks washed out. Which settings should I check?
output: Mark color textures as sRGB, including base color and emissive maps.
Keep roughness, metalness, normal, and ambient occlusion maps in their default non-color space.
Check lighting and environment settings after correcting texture color spaces.

output_examples.input: How should I make a glass object in a product viewer?
output: Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission enabled, low roughness, and zero metalness.
Set thickness and an appropriate index of refraction.
Place opaque objects or a background behind the glass for refraction, and use environment lighting for reflections.

output_examples.input: My custom GLSL material does not work after switching to WebGPURenderer.
output: ShaderMaterial and RawShaderMaterial do not have a direct WebGPURenderer path in this reference.
Use a node-material class from three/webgpu and TSL functions from three/tsl.
Choose an unlit node material for color-only effects, or provide lighting for a lit node material.

best_practices: Check the project renderer and three.js version before applying examples.
Assign texture color spaces and UV channels according to each map's role.
Share materials where appropriate, prefer opaque rendering when possible, and dispose unused materials and textures separately.
anti_patterns: Using lit materials without lights or a suitable environment.
Treating scalar texture maps as sRGB color data.
Assuming WebGL shader materials and line-width settings transfer unchanged to WebGPU.

faq.question: Which three.js version does this skill target?
faq.answer: The reference targets three.js r186. Check API compatibility before using its examples with another release.

faq.question: Which material should I start with for realistic surfaces?
faq.answer: Start with MeshStandardMaterial. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial when you need features such as transmission, clearcoat, or sheen.

faq.question: Does the skill include textures or a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides Markdown guidance and JavaScript examples. You must supply project setup, models, textures, and environment assets.

faq.question: Does it cover WebGPU materials?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes WebGPURenderer initialization, TSL node-material examples, and compatibility notes for materials and point rendering.

faq.question: Why do some surfaces render black?
faq.answer: Lit materials need lights or a suitable environment. Use an unlit material when the effect should not depend on lighting.

faq.question: Can I use this reference with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill lists support for all three tools. It supplies material guidance rather than installing dependencies or running rendering checks.
